summary: Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993 and served there as an associate professor (attested 1996) and later as professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954) and held professorships at Ryukoku University (~1961–1963) and Toyo University (assistant professor ~1958–1967; professor ~1967–1984).

Shōkin Furuta (1911–2001) studied at Shimane University (~1930–1933), working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He directed Matsugaoka Bunko (~1966–2001) and held posts at Hokkaido University and Nihon University (both attested 1998).
Shōkō Kabutogi (b. 1912) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University from ~1932 to 1936 and later served as a professor there from ~1967 to 1983.
Shūei Tsuboi (1914–1989) was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University, with his tenure attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shūichi Katō (1919–2008), active in Japanology and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1943) and held posts there (~1943–1951), UBC (~1960–1969), Free University of Berlin (~1969–1973), Sophia University (~1973–1984), Yale (~1980–1981), and Ritsumeikan University (~1993–2008).

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma. He also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including U Kundala, U Sajjanasāra, and U Sāsana.

Sibani Dasgupta is an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibraj Chetry specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma as well as teachers D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and was Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).
Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen in 1867 and under Albrecht Weber (1864) and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1869).

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1943–1949), held a post at the University of Kiel (~1962–1967), and served as a professor at Stockholm University (attested 1991).

Siglinde Dietz works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Bonn in 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
Signe Howell (1942–2025) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at the University of Oxford (~1975–1980) and held a post at the University of Oslo from ~1987 to 2012.
Sik Fanin works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed a PhD at Lancaster University in 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton. Active in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, he held posts at Naples Federico II, "L'Orientale", Sapienza, Kyoto University of Foreign Studies, and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2002–2017).
Simo Parpola (b. 1943) is a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He served as Professor of Assyriology at the University of Helsinki from ~1979 to 2009.
Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He held posts at Durham University, serving as a tutor in philosophy (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Singhathon Narāsabho works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti (attested 1971).

Siniruddha Dash (b. 1955) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He served as head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014; attested 2022) and was Director of the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (attested 2013).

Sisir Roy specializes in philosophy. He studied under Debabrata SenSharma and held a professorship at the Indian Statistical Institute (attested 2009) as well as a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).
